facets.name: Environmental impact focus
facets.rationale: The keywords across the processed batches distinguish carbon-oriented impacts, energy and power efficiency concerns, water-related burdens, material or waste burdens, biodiversity-related impacts, and a smaller set of papers that frame environmental sustainability in aggregate rather than through one named burden.

categories.name: Carbon emissions and footprint
categories.description: Papers that explicitly address carbon emissions, carbon footprints, decarbonization, operational or embodied carbon, carbon intensity, or greenhouse gas generation.

categories.name: Energy and power efficiency
categories.description: Papers centered on reducing energy demand, improving power efficiency, reusing waste energy, or optimizing electricity use in HPC systems, workloads, cooling, or data movement.

categories.name: Material, waste, and resource burdens
categories.description: Papers that highlight construction waste, e-waste, hardware lifetime or reuse, metal and mineral depletion, procurement-related burdens, or other material-intensive environmental impacts that are distinct from water use and biodiversity impacts.

categories.name: Water use and hydrological impacts
categories.description: Papers that explicitly address water consumption, water footprint, water-efficient cooling, water scarcity, or thermal impacts on water resources from HPC infrastructure.

categories.name: Biodiversity and ecosystem impacts
categories.description: Papers that explicitly address biodiversity loss, ecosystem impacts, or biodiversity-related embodied and operational burdens from HPC facilities, hardware, or workloads.

categories.name: Aggregate environmental impacts
categories.description: Papers that treat HPC sustainability as an aggregate or explicitly multi-impact environmental problem rather than centering one named burden type.

facets.name: Lifecycle stage
facets.rationale: Keywords consistently point to upstream design decisions, operational management, full lifecycle reasoning, and waste-related downstream effects.

categories.name: Upstream planning and procurement
categories.description: Topics concerned with facility planning or siting, hardware design, manufacturing, procurement, replacement, or virtual prototyping before routine operation.

categories.name: Operational use and control
categories.description: Topics addressing the environmental implications of running HPC systems, including scheduling, runtime control, cooling and heat-reuse operations, resource management, reporting, code execution, and data transfer.

categories.name: Whole-system lifecycle
categories.description: Topics that explicitly connect environmental implications across multiple lifecycle stages, such as design, operation, and disposal, instead of treating one stage in isolation.

categories.name: End-of-life and residual materials
categories.description: Topics concerned with waste streams, residual material burdens, or strategies that extend hardware life through reuse, recycling, or aging-aware operation.

facets.name: System locus
facets.rationale: The keywords differentiate where the sustainability problem is situated: in facilities and thermal/energy infrastructure, hardware choices, software and workloads, or operational governance around operators and users.

categories.name: Facility, thermal, and energy infrastructure
categories.description: Topics focused on data centers, siting, cooling systems, heat recovery, district heating links, onsite or distributed power generation, renewable energy integration, grid coupling, or related site-level infrastructure.

categories.name: Compute hardware and procurement
categories.description: Topics focused on hardware components, supercomputer design, server replacement, material composition, alternative compute substrates, or procurement decisions that shape environmental outcomes.

categories.name: Software, workloads, and data flows
categories.description: Topics focused on scheduling, optimization, workload distribution, workload shifting, application and code behavior, or end-to-end movement of data through HPC systems.

categories.name: Operational governance and user practices
categories.description: Topics focused on how operators, users, and policymakers shape environmental performance through incentives, behavior, awareness, reporting, sustainability metrics, and operational or policy management.

facets.name: Management and intervention levers
facets.rationale: The batches use keywords that repeatedly describe how sustainability is acted on: by making impacts visible, controlling runtime behavior, redesigning infrastructure, or changing organizational incentives and strategy.

categories.name: Measurement, accounting, and visibility
categories.description: Papers that make environmental impacts measurable or reportable through accounting frameworks, lifecycle assessment, carbon, energy, water, biodiversity, or material modeling, observability tooling, benchmark datasets, empirical analysis, forecasting, or user-facing reporting.

categories.name: Runtime control and workload optimization
categories.description: Papers that seek lower impact through scheduling, workload shifting, power control, application or code-level optimization, or other runtime management mechanisms.

categories.name: Infrastructure and cooling design
categories.description: Papers that improve sustainability through facility planning or siting, power-supply choices, hardware design or replacement, hardware reuse, cooling choices, waste heat recovery, water-aware cooling, district heating links, or other engineering decisions about infrastructure and compute substrates.

categories.name: Incentives and strategic framing
categories.description: Papers that emphasize sustainability visions, decarbonization roadmaps, user or operator incentives, organizational or policy strategy, or other framing devices for changing behavior.

facets.name: Research type
facets.rationale: The corpus already carries one Wieringa-coded research type per paper in `keywording.csv`. Representing that coding as a facet makes methodological comparisons explicit alongside the topical facets and supports cross-tabulation for RQ2 and RQ3.

categories.name: Validation Research
categories.description: Techniques investigated are novel and have not yet been implemented in practice; evidence is typically produced through experiments or other lab-style studies.

categories.name: Evaluation Research
categories.description: Techniques are implemented in practice and evaluated in terms of their consequences, benefits, or drawbacks, including studies that identify concrete problems in industry settings.

categories.name: Solution Proposal
categories.description: A solution to a problem is proposed as a novel idea or a significant extension of an existing technique, supported by a small example or a clear line of argument for applicability.

categories.name: Philosophical Paper
categories.description: Papers that structure the field through a taxonomy, conceptual framework, or another new way of looking at existing things.

categories.name: Opinion Paper
categories.description: Papers that argue how things should be done or whether a technique is good or bad without grounding the claim in related work and formal research methodology.

categories.name: Experience Paper
categories.description: Papers that explain what was done in practice and how it was done, based on the authors' own operational experience.

schema_notes: The schema now uses 5 facets: 4 topical facets derived from paper keywords plus a Research type facet that mirrors the Wieringa-coded `research_type` values in `artifacts/keywording.csv` to support methodological comparisons. Because Research type is copied from a controlled coding field rather than inferred from keywords, its categories intentionally omit `example_keywords` and rely on category descriptions plus one-to-one classifications. The topical facets still fit the full current corpus without further splitting: aggregate environmental framing remains broad enough to absorb ecological-sensitivity and air-pollution modeling when those concerns are coupled to a carbon-centered analysis, job- and system-level modeling still fits the existing measurement lever, and infrastructure planning, renewable integration, and waste-heat utilization remain cross-cutting themes rather than standalone topical facets. When new papers are added, keep the Research type facet synchronized one-to-one with the `research_type` column.
